What Does a $499 Business Website Actually Include?

By Chronolyte · Updated 2026-10-20

A practical breakdown of pages, forms, SEO foundations, design, launch steps, add-ons and ownership questions for a $499 starter site.

The quick answer

Chronolyte’s $499 starting offer is a complete small-business brochure website for an agreed, limited scope—not a promise of unlimited custom development. The starter scope covers up to five core pages, responsive design, a contact form, basic metadata, domain connection guidance and one consolidated revision round.

Example five-page structure

  • Home: a concise explanation of your services and a contact call to action
  • About: who you help and your approach
  • Services: what customers can book or request
  • Contact: a functional form, email or phone details
  • One additional page: a gallery, FAQ, project examples or service-area information

SEO foundations versus ongoing SEO

Page titles, descriptions, headings, internal links and crawlable content are foundations. They do not automatically create rankings or AI recommendations. Ongoing growth may require original articles, case studies, citations, links and Search Console monitoring.

Which additions increase the price?

  • Long-form copywriting, photography and brand identity
  • Advanced appointments, e-commerce checkouts or customer portals
  • Custom databases, CRM syncs and complicated APIs
  • Additional pages or extensive redesign rounds
  • Paid hosting, domain registrations and third-party subscriptions

The 48-hour and seven-day distinction

Some one-page projects can target 48 hours once ready. The $499 five-page starter website typically targets three to seven days for an eligible project after requirements, copy and approvals are available. Changes of scope and third-party approvals can extend the schedule.

Before paying, confirm these four things

  • The complete written scope and final quote
  • Who controls domain, hosting and handover access
  • Which revisions and support are included
  • How launch approval and payment milestones work

Frequently asked questions

Does a $499 website have multiple pages?

Yes, the advertised Chronolyte starter package includes up to five agreed pages.

Is this a subscription?

The advertised $499 is a starting one-time project price. Domain, hosting and optional maintenance can have separate recurring costs.

Is the price guaranteed?

No. A written quote confirms the scope and total before development begins.
